lean.statement:
∀ {d n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hnd : n ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ)
    (Os : Fin (d / n) → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ),
    let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
      ((Equiv.sumCongr
        ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
        (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
        (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
    let B : Fin (d / n) → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ := fun j =>
      ((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) -
        ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((Os j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) +
          (Os j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose)
    let A := Matrix.reindex e e
      (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.blockDiagonal B) 0 0
        (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ))
    let f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
      (WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x) / 2
    let query : Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Bool →
        EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) := fun j v inverse =>
      WithLp.toLp 2 (if inverse then
        (Os j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp v
      else (Os j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp v)
    let xb : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → Fin (d / n) →
        EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) := fun x j =>
      WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inl (i, j))))
    let gb : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → Fin (d / n) →
        EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) := fun x j =>
      ((κ + 1) / 2) • xb x j - ((κ - 1) / 4) •
        (query j (xb x j) false + query j (xb x j) true)
    let g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) := fun x =>
      WithLp.toLp 2 (fun a => Sum.elim
        (fun ij => gb x ij.2 ij.1)
        (fun i => x (e (Sum.inr i))) (e.symm a))
    ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      HasGradientAt f (g x) x ∧
      (f x, gradient f x) = (inner ℝ x (g x) / 2, g x)
approved_definition_context: EuclideanSpace real (Fin m) is the real m-dimensional inner product space with the l2 norm. Fin m indexes coordinates from zero. WithLp.toLp 2 and WithLp.ofLp preserve entries; inner real is the ordinary real Euclidean inner product.

Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) real is the full group of real orthogonal matrices, containing either determinant sign. A matrix coerced from this group has inverse equal to its transpose. Matrix multiplication by a vector and the dot product are finite sums.

Matrix.reindex e e M has entries M (e.symm i) (e.symm j). Matrix.blockDiagonal B is indexed by pairs (local coordinate, block index) and vanishes between distinct blocks. Matrix.fromBlocks assembles its four displayed blocks. The symbol 1 denotes the identity matrix.

Equiv.prodComm exchanges the factors. finProdFinEquiv sends (a,b) to a times the cardinality of the second factor plus b. finSumFinEquiv concatenates the summands; finCongr transports along its displayed equality of cardinalities. Sum.elim selects the indicated branch.

HasGradientAt f v x means that f has a genuine Frechet derivative at x represented by the inner product with v. The operation gradient f x is totalized: it selects the derivative-representing vector when differentiability holds and otherwise returns zero. The displayed conjunction includes HasGradientAt as a conclusion; this context does not supply it as a premise.

Bool has the two values false and true; the displayed conditional chooses its first branch when true and its second branch when false. Scalar multiplication and real arithmetic have their usual meanings; natural division and remainder are floor division and remainder. A product equality asserts equality of both components.

blind_reconstruction.reconstructed_theorem_text: For every pair of natural numbers d,n with 3 <= n <= d, every real number kappa >= 4, and every family (O_j) indexed by j = 0,...,q-1 of real orthogonal n-by-n matrices, where q = floor(d/n) and r = d mod n, the following holds. Put alpha = (kappa+1)/2 and beta = (kappa-1)/4. Identify the d coordinates with q full blocks of n coordinates followed by r remaining coordinates: the local coordinate i of block j has global coordinate j*n+i, and remaining coordinate i has global coordinate q*n+i. Define B_j = alpha I_n - beta (O_j + O_j^T), let A be the d-by-d matrix with these q diagonal blocks and the identity I_r on the remaining coordinates, with all intervening blocks zero, and define f(x) = (x^T A x)/2 on real Euclidean d-space. For v in real Euclidean n-space define Q(j,v,false) = O_j v and Q(j,v,true) = O_j^T v. For x in real Euclidean d-space, let x_j be its vector of coordinates in full block j and define g_j(x) = alpha x_j - beta (Q(j,x_j,false) + Q(j,x_j,true)). Define g(x) by placing g_j(x) in full block j and copying x on the r remaining coordinates. Then, for every x in real Euclidean d-space, f has a Frechet derivative at x represented by g(x), namely h maps to the Euclidean inner product of g(x) with h, and the simultaneous equality (f(x), gradient f(x)) = ((inner product of x with g(x))/2, g(x)) holds. In particular, the derivative and gradient assertions are conclusions for every x. The orthogonal matrices may have either determinant sign; the assertion is universal over these families.
blind_reconstruction.objects: q = floor(d/n) full blocks and r = d mod n remaining coordinates; a family O_j of real orthogonal n-by-n matrices; the coordinate equivalence e with e(inl(i,j)) = j*n+i and e(inr(i)) = q*n+i; alpha = (kappa+1)/2 and beta = (kappa-1)/4; B_j = alpha I_n - beta(O_j + O_j^T); A = diag(B_0,...,B_(q-1),I_r) under e; f(x) = x^T A x/2; Q(j,v,false) = O_j v and Q(j,v,true) = O_j^T v; full-block extraction x_j; g_j(x) = alpha x_j - beta(Q(j,x_j,false)+Q(j,x_j,true)); g(x) is the assembly of g_j(x) with the unchanged remaining coordinates.
blind_reconstruction.domains: d,n are natural numbers; kappa is real. j ranges over Fin q and full-block coordinate i over Fin n; remaining coordinate i ranges over Fin r, which may be empty. O_j belongs to the full real orthogonal group on n coordinates, allowing either determinant sign. B_j is a real n-by-n matrix, A a real d-by-d matrix, x and g(x) belong to real Euclidean d-space, and v, x_j, Q(j,v,b), and g_j(x) belong to real Euclidean n-space. The inverse selector b belongs to Bool. All inner products and derivatives are over the reals with the ordinary Euclidean inner product.
blind_reconstruction.quantifiers: Universally choose natural d,n subject to 3 <= n and n <= d, then real kappa subject to 4 <= kappa, then every family O : Fin(floor(d/n)) -> O(n). With all displayed let-definitions fixed by those choices, the conclusion holds universally for every x in real Euclidean d-space. The Frechet derivative representation applies to every increment h in that space. There are no existentially chosen matrices, constants, points, or algorithms.
blind_reconstruction.assumptions: The only displayed numerical assumptions are 3 <= n, n <= d, and 4 <= kappa. Every O_j is orthogonal by its declared domain. Thus n and d are positive and q >= 1; r is the natural remainder. The query, block extraction, matrices, function, and vector g are definitions. Differentiability and gradient correctness are not assumptions. No distributional, determinant-sign, initial-point, or nonzero-vector assumption is imposed.
blind_reconstruction.conclusion: For every x, HasGradientAt f (g(x)) x holds: f has a genuine Frechet derivative at x given by h -> <g(x),h>. At the same x, (f(x), gradient f(x)) = (<x,g(x)>/2, g(x)), asserting both f(x) = <x,g(x)>/2 and gradient f(x) = g(x). The vector g(x) uses alpha x_j minus beta times the sum of the forward and transpose query values in each full block, and equals x on the remaining coordinates.
blind_reconstruction.scopes: All local definitions q,r,e,B,A,f,Q,block extraction,g_j,g are under the universal d,n,kappa,O choices; x is universally quantified after those definitions. The family index j selects a full block, the n-coordinate index i stays inside that block, and the remainder branch uses its own Fin r index. Each Boolean choice affects only the indicated matrix multiplication. HasGradientAt and the pair equality are conjoined for the same x and same g(x). The proposition states an exact deterministic identity and derivative representation for all these choices; it contains no separate probabilistic, convergence, optimality, or query-complexity assertion.
blind_reconstruction.constant_dependencies: The fixed numerical thresholds are 3 for n and 4 for kappa; the coefficients 1/2 and 1/4 and identities are explicit. q,r and e depend only on d,n. alpha and beta depend only on kappa. B_j depends on kappa and O_j, with size n. A and f depend on d,n,kappa and the complete family O. Q depends on the selected O_j and its vector and Boolean inputs, with index sets determined by d,n; its formula does not depend on kappa. Block extraction depends on d,n and x. g_j and g depend on d,n,kappa,O and x. The derivative statement and identities hold for every x with the already fixed same data. No unnamed, asymptotic, tolerance-dependent, or existential constants occur.
